newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dlr sneaks higher as market sleeps.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dlr sneaks higher as market sleeps.

text.p: The Australian dollar inched up to its highest level for a fortnight Monday, although dealers said the gains owed more to an illiquid market than real demand.

The currency had begun with an upward bent after bouncing solidly from US$0.7915 late last week to recover the US$0.7950 resistance level, surprising much of the local market which had been short in anticipation of a deeper correction.

Resulting position-squaring resulted in some very modest demand today, but this was still enough to see the currency higher since many banks had already wrapped up business for Christmas and Tokyo was off on its own holiday.
By 4.55 pm (0555 GMT) the local dollar had come to rest at US$0.7962/67 after reaching as high as US$0.7976 from an early US$0.7946/51 and US$0.7956/61 late Friday.
This was the first venture outside the US$0.7910/7970 range established since the surprise cut in domestic interest rates on December 11 toppled it from US$0.8020.

The resilience of support gave bulls some hope the stalled uptrend could resume in the new year, but a break of tough resistance at US$0.8050 was needed for confirmation. While it remained below there, analysts felt there was a real risk the retracement had not ended and a fall to US$0.7810 was possible.
On the crosses it held firm at 90.92/02 yen from 90.89/99 late Friday, mirroring US$/yen which was holding steady above 114.00. In trade weighted terms it ended unchanged from Friday's late 59.2.
There was no local data of note today and Tuesday's offering of motor vehicle registrations was unlikely to liven a market eager to close early for the holiday season.
Analysts generally expect the volatile registrations series to rise around 3.0 percent in November in a natural correction to October's surprisingly steep 5.8 percent fall.
